entries.title: Jude 1:1
segments: Jude. It is generally agreed that the writer of this epistle was one of the four brothers of Jesus, named in

.  The similarity of many passages to the second and third chapters of the Second Epistle of Peter have led to an endeavor to discover one authorship for both, but there is no dependable evidence to support this surmise.
 

 
 Them that are called. The elect.  See note,

entries.title: Jude 1:3
segments: The faith which was once for all delivered. The gospel was delivered not in part but as a complete whole- 'once for all.'  The verses following warn against the perversions of the 'faith' by 'certain men':- doubtless the 'false teachers' spoken of in

entries.title: Jude 1:5
segments: To put you in remembrance, though ye know all things. Through the 'anointing from the Holy One' (
) the faithful believer needed not that any one teach him (
).  Jude's reminder of this is also an admonition to be stedfast.

entries.title: Jude 1:6
segments: Angels that kept not their own principality. It is supposed that these were the 'sons of God' mentioned in

entries.title: Jude 1:8
segments: Defile the flesh, and set at nought dominion. The great error which had come into the Christian church through false teachings seems to have been a perversion of the spiritual 'fervent love' enjoined toward the brethren (
) into lustfulness so gross as to be comparable to the sins of Sodom and Gomorrah, and to the fall of angels from their high estate.  In this condition of 'blackness of darkness' (
) not only was the flesh defiled, but spiritual dominion was set at nought, and its dignities (glories) held in contempt.

entries.title: Jude 1:9
segments: But Michael the archangel when contending with the devil. Jude here seems to refer to a familiar tradition, but no other record of its now remains.

entries.title: Jude 1:14
segments: Enoch, the seventh from Adam. The prophecy here cited is from the Apocryphal Book of Enoch in the words of an angel who thus interpreted a vision.

entries.title: Jude 1:23
segments: And on some have mercy with fear; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh. An injunction to the same caution in the mental sphere as would be exercised toward the very garments of one having a contagious disease.
